claim: Under SYNCHRONOUS updates most of the state space cycles
even_odd (index parity) leaves coupled neurons updating together
value: 19/43 = 44.2% of coupled pairs share a delay; hub neuron 14 (degree 11) collides with 6 of its neighbours

claim: Coupled neurons must differ in DELAY VALUE -- necessary and sufficient
value: colour+commens: 100% settled (3 schemes); colour+incommens: 100% settled (15 schemes); colour+nosep: 0% settled (1 schemes); parity+incommens: 0% settled (1 schemes); across 12 prime permutations sd=0.00
note: colour+distinct settles 100% whether or not delays are commensurate; both controls (identical delays / no colouring) settle 0%

claim: The 'T_ODD/T_EVEN symmetry crisis' is the value-collision rule, not a distinct timing phenomenon
note: ORIGINAL claim was 'avoid integer ratios'. ratio=1.0 means T_ODD==T_EVEN, i.e. ALL neurons share one delay value -- exactly the all_equal control in C3, which settles 0% on hard states. Round 7 shows commensurate delays settle fine (100% on uosc) as long as values DIFFER, so the integer-ratio framing is wrong; only equality matters.

claim: '32 states never converge under any configuration'
note: ORIGINAL claim (finding #4) said these were universal oscillators that no schedule settles. FALSE: every graph-coloured schedule settles all 32 of them. They were artifacts of parity collisions, not intrinsic limit cycles.

claim: 'noise' delay mode is a third independent schedule
note: round(d + U(-0.5,0.5)) almost always returns d, so the canonical noise config emits the depth schedule verbatim. Every 'noise' row in rounds 1-5 duplicates depth. Noise sweeps at scale>=2.0 ARE genuine.

claim: The schedule scales: chi stays ~6 and settling stays 100% as N grows
value: N=1024: chi=5, settled 100%, recall 100%; N=2048: chi=6, settled 100%, recall 100%; N=4096: chi=6, settled 100%, recall 100%
note: Python schedule simulator, validated against SV at N=16. NOT RTL-verified above N=16 -- state this limitation in the paper.

claim: Don't-care minimisation keeps LUT term count flat as fan-in grows
value: fan-in 16: 31-54 terms (vs ~1,000-2,900 fully specified, 34.5x); fan-in 24: 10-58 terms (full table 16.7M rows, infeasible); fan-in 32: 5-27 terms
note: care set = M*sum_{j<=h} C(d,j), polynomial in fan-in. REVERSES the earlier 'LUT area crossover at fan-in 9' estimate, which applied the C(d,d/2) bound to fully-specified tables.

claim: The minimised network is behaviourally identical inside the operating region, and differs outside it
value: N=256 fan-in 16: HD=0/1/3/5 -> 100% settled, 100% recall, 100% agreement with the exact network; uniform random -> 98% settled, 2% agreement
note: The 2% off-region agreement is the real cost of the method and must be reported, not buried: behaviour on far-from-pattern inputs is unspecified.

claim: Recall is governed by loading alpha=M/N, not by the schedule
note: Idealised random-async on UNPRUNED pseudoinverse nets. The alpha trend transfers; absolute numbers do not (the network under test is pruned). Corroborated independently by the pruned pipeline: N=256 fan-in 16 (alpha=0.016) reaches 100% recall.

claim: Once scheduled, failures are spurious attractors rather than oscillation
note: This is what separates the two levers: scheduling fixes settling, loading fixes correctness.

claim: On fully-specified tables espresso tracks the C(d,d/2) threshold bound
value: 5/16 neurons hit the bound exactly (e.g. neuron 7: 9 inputs, 126 terms = C(9,4)); neuron 14: 11 inputs, 386 vs 462
note: This is why FULLY-SPECIFIED LUTs blow up -- and why don't-cares (C8) are the whole story.

claim: The full flow (don't-care SOPs -> SystemVerilog -> iverilog) runs at N=256 and matches the simulator exactly
value: 240 trials (60 each at HD=0,1,3,5): RTL 100% settled, 100% recall; RTL result identical to the simulator on 240/240 inputs; 12,357 product terms over 256 neurons, chi=4, 0 delay-value conflicts
note: This is the T3->T1 upgrade. Scaling above N=16 is no longer simulator-only: the simulator's periodic-firing approximation is confirmed against event-driven NBA semantics at N=256. N>256 remains T3.
